text: This is how the reactor at Chernobyl made electricity, and why it could run away. Uranium atoms split, releasing heat and neutrons that split more atoms. A huge stack of graphite slows those neutrons down, to keep the chain going. Water flows up through the core, boils, and the steam spins a turbine. Boron rods slide in from above to swallow neutrons and control it. But the water also swallows neutrons. Turn it to steam, and the reaction speeds up, which makes more steam. At low power, that loop made it unstable. Full video on my channel.
